baby-toddler-cereal-multigrain-with-frui.title: Baby Toddler cereal, multigrain with fruit, dry

content.title: About
content.content: Baby Toddler cereal is a dry infant food made from a blend of whole grains (oats, rice, wheat) and natural fruit pieces. It is intended for children from 6 months old. Easy to prepare, it dissolves quickly in warm milk or water, creating a smooth, fragrant porridge.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Contains three types of whole grains, providing a varied nutrient profile.
Fruit pieces are made from apples, pears and berries with no added sugar.
Product meets strict quality controls and complies with European infant‑food standards.
Packaging is recyclable and features a convenient dispenser.
The cereal includes natural wheat gluten, not gluten‑free substitutes.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole grains supply fiber that supports healthy digestion in toddlers.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Oats and rice provide vitamins B1, B2 and B6, aiding energy metabolism.

items.title: Natural antioxidants
items.content: Fruit pieces contain vitamin C and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Minerals for growth
items.content: The formula includes iron, zinc and magnesium, essential for bone and nervous system development.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Sweetness comes from natural fruit sugars, without refined sugar addition.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The product contains wheat; children with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should use a gluten‑free alternative.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Dry granules can pose a choking risk for infants under 12 months – always prepare the cereal to a fully soft consistency.

items.title: Post‑opening storage
items.content: After opening, keep the package sealed in a dry place and use within 30 days to prevent mold growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix the cereal with 200 ml of warm (not boiling) milk or water, stir, and let it sit for 2–3 minutes. Adjust liquid to achieve the desired consistency. Optional: add fruit puree or a spoonful of infant‑friendly yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal the bag tightly and use within a month.

content.title: About
content.content: Biscayne codfish is a warm‑water Caribbean fish prized for its firm white flesh. In Puerto Rican style it is marinated with lime, garlic, olive oil and aromatic spices, then quickly seared or baked, resulting in a tender, mildly tangy dish that is a staple of island cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Biscayne cod is a common ingredient in traditional Puerto Rican dishes such as pasteles and mofongo.
The fish’s dense white meat readily absorbs marinades and seasonings.
It is often served with rice, beans and fried plantains as a classic plate.
Compared with Atlantic cod, Biscayne cod has a lower environmental impact due to faster growth rates.
Fresh fillets are sold in local markets, but frozen portions are widely available.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Provides essential amino acids needed for muscle maintenance and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Contains very little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin B12
items.content: Supports nerve function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and supports immune health.

items.title: Contains omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Provides modest amounts of EPA and DHA, beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals with seafood allergies may react to codfish.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Like many marine species, cod can accumulate mercury; moderate consumption is advised, especially for pregnant women and children.

items.title: Nutrient loss with overcooking
items.content: Excessive heat can degrade vitamin B12 and omega‑3 fatty acids.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Marinate the fillets in lime juice, minced garlic, olive oil and spices (paprika, oregano, cumin), then sear quickly in a hot pan or bake at 200 °C for 10‑12 minutes. Serve with rice, beans, fried plantains or an avocado salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh cod in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped tightly, and use within 2 days. Frozen cod should be stored at –18 °C and consumed within 3‑4 months. Thaw frozen fillets in the fridge, not at room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: Dark chocolate candy is made from cocoa mass, sugar and sometimes added ingredients such as nuts, dried fruit or spices. It contains at least 70 % cocoa, giving it an intense, slightly bitter flavor and a distinctive aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dark chocolate is considered the purest form of chocolate because it contains minimal dairy components.
The cocoa mass used in dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids, which may have antioxidant effects.
The tradition of making chocolate candies originated in Mexico, where cocoa was used in ceremonial drinks.
Dark chocolate is often used in cooking for sauces, mousses and baked goods.
In many countries dark chocolate is marketed as a "healthier" sweet option when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Rich in flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids help combat free radicals, supporting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports muscle and nerve function as well as blood sugar regulation.

items.title: Lower sugar content
items.content: Compared with milk chocolate, dark chocolate usually contains less sugar, making it more suitable for glucose control.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Cocoa mass provides iron, essential for hemoglobin formation.

items.title: Mood‑boosting
items.content: The presence of theobromine and small amounts of caffeine can improve mood and increase alertness.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Dark chocolate is calorie‑dense, so portion sizes should be moderated.

items.title: Caffeine and theobromine content
items.content: Large amounts may cause insomnia or heart palpitations in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to cocoa components.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Cocoa contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in predisposed persons.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dark chocolate candy can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to granola, yogurt, desserts, or used in baking. For a smoother taste, gently melt the pieces and drizzle over fruit.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the candy in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator to prevent melting and fat oxidation. Keep away from strong odors.

frozen-yogurt-cone-vanilla-waffle-cone.title: Frozen yogurt cone, vanilla, waffle cone

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen yogurt cone is a yogurt‑based frozen dessert with a gentle vanilla flavor, served in a crisp waffle cone. The light, creamy texture of the yogurt pairs with the sweet, crunchy shell, creating a pleasant contrast of taste and mouthfeel.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frozen yogurt typically contains less fat than traditional ice cream thanks to its yogurt base.
Vanilla flavor is often derived from natural vanilla beans, but many commercial products use synthetic vanillin.
Waffle cones add extra crunch and can be made with whole‑grain flour for a healthier option.
The yogurt component provides probiotics that support gut health.
Serving ice cream in a cone became popular in the United States in the early 20th century.

items.title: Rich in probiotics
items.content: The yogurt base contains live cultures that help maintain a healthy digestive microbiome.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with regular ice cream, frozen yogurt usually has less saturated fat.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Yogurt provides a good amount of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The yogurt base raises blood sugar more slowly than typical ice cream.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains milk sugar, so those with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein or whey proteins.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Despite lower fat, sugar may be added, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Cone fragility
items.content: Waffle cones can soften quickly if held for long, increasing the risk of breakage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready to eat straight from the package. Enjoy it as a standalone treat, or top with fresh berries, nuts, or a drizzle of fruit sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once removed from the wrapper, consume within 2–3 days to keep the cone crisp.

content.title: About
content.content: Infant Formula NFS (317) is intended for babies from birth to 12 months. It contains fully hydrolysed proteins, prebiotics, DHA, ARA and essential vitamins and minerals, providing a balanced nutrition during early development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula is developed according to WHO and EFSA recommendations.
Fully hydrolysed proteins reduce the risk of allergy in infants with a predisposition to food allergies.
It includes prebiotics (GOS/FOS) that support a healthy gut microbiota.
DHA and ARA are long‑chain omega‑3 and omega‑6 fatty acids important for brain and eye development.
The product undergoes strict quality control and certification to meet international standards.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: A balanced blend of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals meets the nutritional needs of a growing infant.

items.title: Reduces allergy risk
items.content: Hydrolysed proteins are less allergenic, helping to prevent food‑related allergic reactions.

items.title: Gut health
items.content: Prebiotics promote the growth of beneficial bacteria, improving digestion and immunity.

items.title: Brain and eye development
items.content: DHA and ARA are building blocks for neuronal cells and the retina.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D and zinc help maintain the body’s defence mechanisms.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Despite hydrolysis, some infants may still react to milk proteins.

items.title: Incorrect reconstitution
items.content: Over‑concentrated formula can cause hyperosmolarity, while overly diluted formula may lack essential nutrients.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Prepared formula should be used within 48 hours and stored in the refrigerator.

items.title: Temperature control
items.content: Formula that is too hot or too cold can damage nutrients and cause discomfort for the baby.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Mix the powder with freshly boiled water, cool to body temperature (≈37 °C), and stir until smooth. Follow the exact ratio indicated on the packaging.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. After opening, keep it refrigerated and use within 48 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Canned vegetable soup is a ready‑to‑eat product containing a blend of cooked vegetables, broth, and spices, sealed in an airtight can. The thermal processing preserves flavor and nutrients for long‑term storage.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning allows the soup to be stored for several years without refrigeration.
Typical ingredients include carrots, potatoes, onions, celery, and tomatoes, providing a good source of vitamins A and C.
Such soups originated in Europe in the 19th century as a way to preserve seasonal vegetables.
Cans are usually sterilized at 121 °C for 30‑45 minutes.
Canned soups are popular among hikers and in emergency kits because of their lightweight and convenience.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: The vegetables supply vitamins A, C, and B‑complex, supporting immunity and vision.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Most vegetable cans contain little fat, making them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Electrolytes
items.content: Sodium and potassium in the broth help maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Convenient and time‑saving
items.content: A ready‑to‑heat soup saves cooking time, which is useful for busy schedules.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned soups often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Bisphenol A in packaging
items.content: Some metal cans are lined with epoxy resins that may contain BPA; choose BPA‑free labeled products.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Certain recipes may include spices or additives that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Loss of some vitamins
items.content: Heat processing can reduce heat‑sensitive vitamins, such as vitamin C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the soup in a pot or microwave until boiling; optionally stir in fresh herbs, cream, or croutons. It can also serve as a base for more elaborate dishes by adding meat, beans, or grains.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3‑4 days.
